1.title: Optimize Model Performance
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Optimize Model Performance. It covers the exam area Model the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Improve performance by identifying and removing unnecessary rows and columns. Identify poorly performing measures, relationships, and visuals by using Performance Analyzer and dacks query view. Improve performance by reducing granularity. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Model the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Remove unnecessary rows and columns
1.text: Remove unnecessary rows and columns. An Import model is stored in the Verti Paq engine, which compresses data about ten times. A smaller model refreshes faster, takes less memory and answers queries faster. The best savings come from loading less data, and you do the work in Power Query so the steps run at the source when they can.

1.title: Remove unnecessary rows and columns, continued
1.text: Remove unnecessary rows and columns. The figure shows this: A model before and after tuning: fewer columns, fewer rows, a summary table, and a star schema.

1.title: Remove unnecessary rows and columns, continued
1.text: Remove unnecessary rows and columns. Remove columns (vertical filtering). Drop every column that no visual, measure or relationship uses. Filter rows (horizontal filtering). Load only the rows you need, such as recent history with a relative date filter or a parameter. Group and summarize. Aggregate to a coarser grain, such as one row per day and product instead of one per transaction. Choose data types. Numbers compress better with value encoding than text does with hash encoding; fewer distinct values compress better.

1.title: Remove unnecessary rows and columns, continued
1.text: Remove unnecessary rows and columns. Custom columns in Power Query. Prefer them to dacks calculated columns, which cost more memory. Disable auto date or time. Removes a hidden date table for every date column. Disable load for staging queries. Clear Enable load on intermediate queries so they are not loaded into the model.

1.title: Remove unnecessary rows and columns, continued
1.text: Remove unnecessary rows and columns. A staging query is a query that other queries use as a source. It still runs, but its table is not stored in the model. Keep high-cardinality text, such as free-form comments or unique identifiers that nothing uses, out of the model. Exam tip: Vertical filtering removes columns; horizontal filtering removes rows. To shrink a model, filter rows and remove columns in Power Query first. A page or visual filter does not make the model smaller. Exam tip: Prefer Power Query custom columns to dacks calculated columns, disable auto date or time, and clear Enable load on staging queries. Numbers compress better than text.

1.title: Performance Analyzer
1.text: Performance Analyzer. Performance Analyzer records how long each visual takes to load. In Power B I Desktop, open the Optimize tab and choose Performance analyzer. You can also use it when you edit a report in the service. one. Open Performance analyzer and choose Start recording. two. Interact with the report, or choose Refresh visuals. three. Choose Stop, then expand each visual to read its durations. four. Use Copy query, Run in dacks query view, or export the log as a Jason file. Each visual logs four durations.

1.title: Performance Analyzer, continued
1.text: Performance Analyzer. dacks query. Meaning: Time for the model to run the query. If it is high: Tune the measure or the model design, such as relationships. Direct query. Meaning: Time for a Direct Query source to answer. If it is high: Tune the source, query folding or indexes. Visual display. Meaning: Time to draw the visual. If it is high: Too many data points or a heavy custom visual.

1.title: Performance Analyzer, continued
1.text: Performance Analyzer. Other. Meaning: Time spent on other work, such as waiting for other visuals. If it is high: Too many visuals on one page.

1.title: Performance Analyzer, continued
1.text: Performance Analyzer. Performance Analyzer therefore points to the slow visual, to a slow measure when the dacks query time is high, and to a slow relationship when queries across a bi-directional or many-to-many relationship are slow. Copying the query lets you test it in isolation. Exam tip: The four durations are dacks query, Direct query, Visual display and Other. A high dacks query time points to the measure or model, a high Direct query time to the source, and a high Other time to too many visuals.

1.title: DAX query view
1.text: dacks query view. dacks query view lets you write and run dacks queries against the semantic model. Open it from the left navigation in Power B I Desktop, or paste a query that you copied from Performance Analyzer.

1.title: DAX query view, continued
1.text: dacks query view. evaluate. Required; returns a table as the result. define. Optional; defines measures, variables or columns for this query only. define M E A S U R E. Lets you test a changed measure without touching the model. Update model with changes. Writes the measures you defined into the model. Quick queries. Right-click a table or column: show the top one hundred rows, column statistics, define all measures. Limits. Desktop: fifteen megabytes or one million values per query; web: ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine rows.

1.title: DAX query view, continued
1.text: dacks query view. A common workflow is to copy the slow query from Performance Analyzer, run it in dacks query view, rewrite the measure in a define block, and compare the result and the time. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Every dacks query needs evaluate; define is optional. define M E A S U R E changes nothing in the model until you choose Update model with changes.

1.title: Reduce granularity and design for speed
1.text: Reduce granularity and design for speed. Granularity is the level of detail of a table. Fewer, coarser rows mean less data to scan. Summary table. A table you build at a coarser grain, such as daily instead of per transaction, for visuals that do not need the detail. User-defined aggregation. An Import table at a coarser grain, mapped to the detail table with Manage aggregations; queries use it when they can and the detail table otherwise. Automatic aggregations. Power B I builds and maintains aggregations for a Direct Query model for you, based on how reports query it.

2.title: Reduce granularity and design for speed, continued
2.text: Reduce granularity and design for speed. Hybrid table. One table with Import partitions for older data and a Direct Query partition for the newest data. Dual storage mode. A shared dimension that can act as Import or Direct Query, depending on the query. Model design matters just as much. Use a star schema with one-to-many relationships from dimensions to facts, and avoid bi-directional and many-to-many relationships. Relationships run fastest as one-to-many, then many-to-many through a bridge table, then plain many-to-many, and relationships across source groups are the slowest. Use integer key columns.

2.title: Reduce granularity and design for speed, continued
2.text: Reduce granularity and design for speed. Import. Fast: data sits in memory and visuals are fully interactive. Direct Query. Each visual sends queries to the source, so speed depends on the source; needs query folding. Exam tip: Reduce granularity with summary or aggregation tables, and let hybrid tables or automatic aggregations handle large Direct Query data. A one-to-many star schema is faster than bi-directional or many-to-many relationships.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A model holds ten years of sales, but the reports use only the last three years. The file is large and refresh is slow. What should you do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Filter the rows in Power Query to the last three years. Filtering rows before load shrinks the model, whereas page filters, hidden fields and calculated tables leave the full data in it.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. In Performance Analyzer one visual shows a long dacks query duration and a short visual display duration. What should you do next? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Copy the query and test it in dacks query view. A long dacks query duration points to the measure or the model, and dacks query view lets you test and tune the copied query.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A page has thirty visuals. Each visual shows a short dacks query duration but a long Other duration in Performance Analyzer. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The visuals wait for each other to load. The Other duration includes time spent waiting for other operations such as other visuals, so the page needs fewer visuals.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. An author wants to test a changed definition of a measure and see the result as a table without editing the model. What should the author write? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A define M E A S U R E block followed by evaluate. dacks query view runs a define M E A S U R E block with evaluate and leaves the model unchanged.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A Direct Query model over a very large sales table is slow on monthly summary visuals. Which change improves the speed the most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Add an Import aggregation table at a coarser grain. An aggregation table answers summary queries from memory and sends only detail queries to the source.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Two large tables are joined with a many-to-many relationship that filters in both directions, and visuals are slow. What is the best redesign? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Use a star schema with one-to-many relationships. One-to-many relationships from dimensions to facts are the fastest, and bi-directional many-to-many relationships are the slow case.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are vertical filtering and horizontal filtering? Answer: Removing columns and removing rows. Question two. Which setting keeps a staging query out of the model? Answer: Clear Enable load. Question three. What are the four Performance Analyzer durations? Answer: dacks query, Direct query, Visual display and Other.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which statement is required in every dacks query? Answer: evaluate. Question five. Which compresses better, numbers or text? Answer: Numbers, through value encoding. Question six. On which tab do you open Performance Analyzer in Power B I Desktop? Answer: The Optimize tab.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Rows and columns: Remove columns (vertical) and filter rows (horizontal) in Power Query. Smaller model: Group and summarize, numbers over text, custom columns over calculated columns, auto date or time off, Enable load off for staging. Performance Analyzer: Optimize tab; Start recording, interact, Stop; dacks query, Direct query, Visual display, Other. Actions: Copy query, Run in dacks query view, export Jason. dacks query view: evaluate required, define optional; Update model with changes; quick queries. Granularity: Summary tables, user-defined and automatic aggregations, hybrid tables, dual mode. Design: Star schema, one-to-many, avoid bi-directional and many-to-many. Storage mode: Import is fast; Direct Query depends on the source and needs query folding.
